Stimulus:

ScenarioEvidenceClassification clue
Ice meltsSolid water becomes liquid waterNo new substance

Copper conducts electricityCurrent passes through copperProperty observed without changing identity

Question: Which scenario is a physical change?

feedback.text: Melting changes state but water remains water.
Rusting forms iron oxide.
Burning forms new substances.
Souring involves chemical changes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CHEM_U01_L06_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CHEM.MAT.02

Stimulus:

ScenarioEvidenceClassification clue
Ice meltsSolid water becomes liquid waterNo new substance
Iron rustsIron oxide formsNew substance
Copper conducts electricityCurrent passes through copperProperty observed without changing identity

Question: Why is iron rusting a chemical change?

feedback.text: Shape change alone would be physical.

answer.text: A new substance, iron oxide, forms.

feedback.text: Formation of iron oxide means identity changed.

answer.text: The iron is still pure iron.

feedback.text: Rust is not pure iron.
Rusting is not a simple state change.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CHEM_U01_L06_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CHEM.MAT.02

Stimulus:

ScenarioEvidenceClassification clue
Ice meltsSolid water becomes liquid waterNo new substance
Iron rustsIron oxide formsNew substance
Copper conducts electricityCurrent passes through copperProperty observed without changing identity

Question: Why is color change alone not always proof of chemical change?

answer.text: Color can change from mixing or spreading without a new substance.

feedback.text: Color can be evidence, but context determines whether a new substance formed.
Color can be useful when combined with other evidence.

answer.text: All color changes are physical only.

feedback.text: Some color changes are chemical, but not all.

answer.text: Color replaces the need for context.

feedback.text: Context is still required.
